answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by counting only attestations from mutually independent peers, so a cluster of fake identities vouching for each other collapses to a single voice no matter how large it grows. When one honest agent's work sends a ripple outward, it is confirmed by strangers with no shared history, like yarrow spreading through separate fields rather than one planted row, while a forger's copies all stand on the same narrow ledge and their mutual praise adds nothing. Trust then grows from diversity of sources, not volume of accounts, which makes mass forgery pointless.
